findings.title: Required applicant documents remain unreadable
findings.summary: The audited passport preview and HTTPS Open document fallback were exercised, but both viewers appeared black in screenshot capture. Readability could not be verified; a product failure has not been established. The legacy fallback remained black after a ten-minute settling period; a different controlled private fixture rendered legibly in the approval role, indicating fixture-specific coverage remains unresolved.
steps: Open an assigned applicant review and provide the required audit reason for passport evidence.
Use Open document to follow the authorized HTTPS fallback.
Inspect the captured viewer; no readable document content was obtained.

evidence.label: Fallback viewer capture; readability remains unverified
Legacy fallback remained unreadable after settling

findings.limitations: Visual verification/tooling blocker. No claim that the underlying document is defective; authorized document URLs and private identifiers are not published.

findings.title: Unique exact queue search returns the same applicant three times
findings.summary: The current Pending queue contains 22 rows with 22 unique KYC records and 22 unique canonical applicants. Two same-name search results belong to different applicants, not duplicate queue records.
steps: Load all five Pending queue pages through the browser UI: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 2 rows.
Correlate the UI-triggered queue GET responses read-only and verify 22 unique KYC record identities and 22 unique canonical applicant identities.
Compare the two same-name search results and confirm their canonical applicants differ.

evidence.label: Sanitized current Pending queue canonical reconciliation

findings.limitations: Current Pending queue only. New duplicate creation, resubmission and all other statuses were not tested. Raw queue responses and applicant identifiers are not published. Queue-action responsive evidence is separate under F002, not six-size duplicate-proof coverage.

findings.title: Stale member state redirects reviewer login to the wrong portal
findings.summary: An authenticated member session navigated directly to reviewer sign-in, then reviewer login opened the correct dashboard and survived reload.
steps: Sign in as the controlled Pitcher member and open its dashboard.
In the same Chrome context, navigate directly to /kyc-login.
Sign in as reviewer; verify the reviewer dashboard opens.
Reload and verify the reviewer dashboard persists.

evidence.label: Reviewer queue after successful portal transition and reload

findings.limitations: One functional portal-transition journey verified. The authentication journey was not repeated independently at six sizes.
